    <heading id="h-0005">DETAILED DESCRIPTION</heading>
    <div id="p-0021" num="0020" class="description-paragraph">Disclosed embodiments generally relate to systems and methods for filtering materials from biologic fluids of a human or animal subject. In certain implementations, a tangential flow filter may be used to separate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) into permeate and retentate. The permeate may be returned to the subject. In certain implementations, the retentate may be filtered again, for example, through one or more additional tangential flow filters or through different methods of filtering. During operation of the system, various parameters may be modified, such as flow rate and pressure. Certain systems and methods described herein may be combined with other systems and methods for conditioning, removing, or otherwise processing biological materials, such as those discussed in U.S. Pat. No. 8,435,204, which is hereby incorporated by reference.</div>
    <div id="p-0022" num="0021" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>1</b> </figref> illustrates a system <b>100</b> for the filtration of materials from biologic fluids according to certain embodiments, including a filtration system <b>102</b>, an intake <b>104</b>, a retentate outlet <b>106</b>, a permeate outlet <b>108</b>, a vessel <b>110</b>, a reservoir <b>112</b>, and tubing <b>114</b>. The arrows represent an example direction that fluid may take through the system.</div>
    <div id="p-0023" num="0022" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, the filtration system <b>102</b> is a device or combination of devices that is configured to filter, concentrate, dialyze, separate, or otherwise treat or condition the contents of a fluid. The filtration system <b>102</b> may be a tangential flow filtration system (for example, as shown and described in relation to <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>2</b> </figref>) or other system configured to filter fluid. In certain embodiments, the filtration system <b>102</b> receives the fluid through the intake <b>104</b> and separates the fluid into retentate and permeate. The retentate exits the filtration system <b>102</b> through a retentate outlet <b>106</b>, and the permeate exits the filtration system <b>102</b> through a permeate outlet <b>108</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0024" num="0023" class="description-paragraph">The intake <b>104</b> may be a port through which fluid enters the filtration system <b>102</b>. The retentate outlet <b>106</b> may be an outlet through which retentate exits the filtration system <b>102</b>. The permeate outlet <b>108</b> may be an outlet through which permeate exists the filtration system <b>102</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0025" num="0024" class="description-paragraph">The intake <b>104</b>, retentate outlet <b>106</b>, and permeate outlet <b>108</b> may be any kind of ports through which material or fluid may flow. These components may be configured to be in fluid connection by tubing <b>114</b>. The components <b>104</b>, <b>106</b>, <b>108</b>, <b>114</b> may include various fittings to facilitate the connection, including but not limited to compression fittings, flare fittings, bite fittings, quick connection fittings, Luer-type fittings, threaded fittings, and other components configured to enable fluid or other connection between two or more components. In addition to fittings, the components <b>104</b>, <b>106</b>, <b>108</b>, <b>114</b> may also include various elements to facilitate use of the system <b>100</b>, including but not limited to various valves, flow regulators, adapters, converters, stopcocks, reducers, and other elements.</div>
    <div id="p-0026" num="0025" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, there may be one or more permeate outlets <b>108</b> and one or more retentate outlets <b>106</b>. For example, the systems <b>100</b>, <b>300</b> illustrated in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. <b>1</b> and <b>3</b> </figref>, respectively, include a filtration system <b>102</b> having two permeate outlets <b>108</b>. This configuration may facilitate the use of different filtration systems within a filtration system <b>102</b>, <b>302</b>. For example, the filtration systems <b>102</b>, <b>302</b> may include multiple filtration components, each with their own individual outlets.</div>
    <div id="p-0027" num="0026" class="description-paragraph">The vessel <b>110</b> may be a container for storing fluid. For example, fluid leaving the filtration system <b>102</b> may be deposited in the vessel <b>110</b>. The fluid deposited in the vessel <b>110</b> may be held for storage, waste disposal, processing, testing, or other uses. The vessel <b>110</b> may also be a reservoir for subsequent filtering, for example, through the same or different set of filters. This fluid may or not be combined with previously filtered fluid.</div>
    <div id="p-0028" num="0027" class="description-paragraph">The reservoir <b>112</b> may contain a particular fluid to be filtered. In certain implementations, the reservoir <b>112</b> may be an anatomical entity or location within a human or animal subject, such as a chamber or CSF-containing space or a blood vessel. The reservoir <b>112</b> may be the source of the fluid, the destination of the fluid, or both. For example, the system <b>100</b> may remove or receive a volume of fluid from the reservoir <b>112</b>, perform filtration and/or other treatment, and return a portion of the processed and/or treated fluid to the reservoir <b>112</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0029" num="0028" class="description-paragraph">The various components of the system <b>100</b> may be connected through tubing <b>114</b>. For instance, in certain embodiments, there may be a length of the tubing <b>114</b> placing the reservoir <b>112</b> in fluid connection with the intake <b>104</b>. The permeate outlet <b>108</b> may be in fluid connection with the reservoir <b>112</b> via a length of the tubing <b>114</b>. The retentate outlet <b>106</b> may be in fluid connection with the vessel <b>110</b> via a length of the tubing <b>114</b>. The tubing <b>114</b> may be any kind of system for transporting or containing fluid. While the connections within the system <b>100</b> are shown as being direct, the connections need not be. The various portions of the system <b>100</b> may be connected through combinations of connections and various tubing <b>114</b>. In certain embodiments, the tubing <b>114</b> and other portions of the system <b>100</b> may be filled with priming fluid (e.g., saline). Longer lengths of tubing <b>114</b> may correspondingly comprise a larger amount of priming fluid; however, in certain implementations, larger amounts of priming fluid may result in an undesirable amount of dilution of “natural” fluid, such as CSF. Accordingly, in certain implementations, the tubing <b>114</b> may be selected in order to minimize the volume of priming fluid needed, while still having the system be practically useful (e.g., enough tubing to enable the system <b>100</b> to be used at a subject's bedside). Depending on the subject and the reservoir <b>112</b>, the tolerance for removal or dilution of fluid may vary, and the system <b>100</b> may be scaled accordingly. For example, the parameters of the system <b>100</b> may be changed to scale to suit subjects ranging from a mouse to a human or larger mammal.</div>
    <div id="p-0030" num="0029" class="description-paragraph">In certain implementations, the tubing <b>114</b> may have a port <b>124</b> to access the fluid traveling within the tubing <b>114</b>. As illustrated in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>1</b> </figref>, there is a port <b>124</b> between the permeate outlet <b>108</b> and the reservoir <b>112</b>. This port <b>124</b> may be configured for the introduction of additives, such as therapeutic agents, artificial fluid (such as artificial CSF), and/or other additives. The port <b>124</b> may also be configured for the removal of fluid for testing or other purposes. For example, in certain embodiments, fluid returning to the reservoir <b>112</b> may be removed and tested for particular characteristics or parameters. In certain embodiments, tubing <b>114</b> that links the reservoir <b>112</b> to the intake <b>104</b> may include a port <b>124</b>. This port <b>124</b> may also be used for the introduction of additives and/or the removal of fluid. In certain implementations, instead of or in addition to a port <b>124</b> located on the tubing <b>114</b>, there may also be a port <b>122</b> located on the filtration system <b>102</b> itself. This port <b>122</b> may be used to access the fluid within the filtration system <b>102</b> at various points during filtration for various purposes. For example, like the port <b>124</b>, the port <b>122</b> may be used to introduce additives to the system <b>100</b> or remove fluid therefrom. In some embodiments, the ports <b>122</b>, <b>124</b> may be used to link the system <b>100</b> with other systems.</div>
    <div id="p-0031" num="0030" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>2</b>A</figref> illustrates a system and method for withdrawing a fluid <b>202</b> from and returning fluid to the reservoir <b>112</b>, according to certain implementations. The connection between the system <b>100</b> and anatomical structures (such as the reservoir <b>112</b>) may be made in a variety of ways. For example, if the reservoir <b>112</b> is an anatomical location within a subject, as shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>2</b>A</figref>, the connection with the reservoir <b>112</b> may be made through one or more catheters inserted into particular anatomical locations. For example, the catheter may be a multi-lumen catheter inserted through a single opening in the subject to access the anatomical location or may be two catheters inserted at two different, but connected anatomical locations. In certain implementations, the connection may be made via an external ventricular drain system. For example, the tip of a catheter may be placed in a lateral ventricle of the brain.</div>
    <div id="p-0032" num="0031" class="description-paragraph">As a specific example, the certain implementations shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>2</b>A</figref> include a portion of a subject's spine <b>200</b>, including vertebrae <b>201</b>, carrying a fluid <b>202</b> (for example, a fluid comprising CSF), and a multi-lumen catheter <b>204</b>. The multi-lumen catheter <b>204</b> may comprise a first port <b>206</b> and a second port <b>208</b> that place the reservoir <b>112</b> in fluid connection with tubing <b>114</b>. As illustrated, a first volume of the fluid <b>202</b> enters the multi-lumen catheter <b>204</b> through the first port <b>206</b> and is passed through into a portion of the tubing <b>114</b> (for example, a portion of tubing <b>114</b> leading to the intake <b>104</b>). A second volume of fluid <b>202</b> enters the multi-lumen catheter <b>204</b> from a portion of the tubing <b>114</b> (for example, a portion of tubing <b>114</b> coming from the permeate outlet <b>108</b>) and exits the multi-lumen catheter <b>204</b> through the second port <b>208</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0033" num="0032" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>2</b>B</figref> illustrates a system and method for withdrawing fluid from and returning fluid to the reservoir <b>112</b>, according to certain implementations. In this particular example, the multi-lumen catheter <b>204</b> is placed in fluid connection with the ventricles of a subject's brain <b>210</b> in a configuration typically referred to as an external ventricular drain.</div>
    <div id="p-0034" num="0033" class="description-paragraph">Although <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIGS. <b>2</b>A and <b>2</b>B</figref> illustrate accessing CSF in a portion of the spine <b>200</b> and a portion of the brain <b>210</b>, respectively, the embodiments disclosed herein need not be limited to those regions or that fluid and may be used with other locations and fluids. For example, one or more single-lumen catheters may be used to transport the fluid <b>202</b>. As another example, the anatomical location may be a blood vessel and the fluid may be blood.</div>
    <div id="p-0035" num="0034" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>2</b>C</figref> illustrates a block diagram of a filtration system <b>102</b> according to certain embodiments, with solid arrows indicating an example flow path for fluids and materials, and dashed arrows indicating an example flow path for signals and information. <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>2</b>C</figref> illustrates the intake <b>104</b>, the retentate outlet <b>106</b>, the permeate outlet <b>108</b>, a pump <b>222</b>, a sensor <b>224</b>, a filter <b>226</b>, a processing unit <b>228</b>, and an interface <b>230</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0036" num="0035" class="description-paragraph">The pump <b>222</b> may be any device for inducing fluid flow through one or more portions of the filtration system <b>102</b>. In certain embodiments, the pump <b>222</b> may be a peristaltic pump, which may reduce the need for sterilization of complex pump components; however, other types of pumps may be used. The operation of the pump <b>222</b> may be controlled by modifying the operating parameters of the pump <b>222</b>. This may enable the flow rate, pressure, and/or other parameters of the pump <b>222</b> to be changed. The pump <b>222</b> may also be used to withdraw the fluid from the reservoir <b>112</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0037" num="0036" class="description-paragraph">The sensor <b>224</b> may be a device for generating and/or receiving information, including but not limited to one or more of characteristics of the fluid withdrawn from the reservoir <b>112</b>, before, after, and/or during filtration, including but not limited to temperature; pressure; the ratio of permeate volume to retentate volume; the fluid flow rate to and/or from the reservoir <b>112</b>; the amount of contaminants or other materials in the fluid; the fluid flow return rate; the filter efficiency; filter status (for example, whether the filters are clogged or otherwise running inefficiently); and other parameters or characteristics. While the sensor <b>224</b> is shown within the filtration system <b>102</b>, one or more sensors <b>224</b> may be located elsewhere in the system <b>100</b> and/or cooperate with other locations. The sensor <b>224</b> may convert the data into computer- and/or human-readable representations for processing.</div>
    <div id="p-0038" num="0037" class="description-paragraph">The filter <b>226</b> may be a device for separating a first portion of materials and/or fluid from a second portion of materials and/or fluid. The design and type of the filter <b>226</b> may vary depending on the type of fluid and the desired filtration results. For example, the filter <b>226</b> may be a tangential flow filter configured to separate the fluid into permeate and retentate (see, for example, <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>2</b>D</figref>) with the retentate flowing to the retentate outlet <b>106</b> and the permeate flowing to the permeate outlet <b>108</b>. For example, various combinations of filters may be used to achieve different kinds of filtration. For example, the filters may include filters of various pore sizes and different attributes. For example, filtering schemes may include ultrafiltration, microfiltration, macrofiltration and other sized filters that have various porosities. Combinations of filters may include dead end filtration, depth filtration, tangential flow filtration, affinity filtration, centrifugal filtration, vacuum filtration, and/or combinations thereof. Multiple filtration systems may be useful in order to continually re-filter retentate in order to yield a higher volume of permeate that may be returned to the reservoir <b>112</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0039" num="0038" class="description-paragraph">The processing unit <b>228</b> may be a device configured to control the operation of the filtration system <b>102</b>, for example by sending signals to the pump <b>222</b>, sensor <b>224</b>, and/or filter <b>226</b>. In some embodiments, the signals are sent in response to receiving input from the interface <b>210</b>. In certain embodiments, the processing unit <b>228</b> may be processing information, such as data received from the sensor <b>224</b> and/or the interface <b>210</b> and making decisions based on the information. In certain embodiments, the processing unit <b>228</b> may itself make decisions based on the information. For example, the processing unit <b>228</b> may include a processor and memory for running instructions configured to receive input, make decisions, and provide output.</div>
    <div id="p-0040" num="0039" class="description-paragraph">The interface <b>230</b> may be a device or system of devices configured to receive input and/or provide output. In certain embodiments, the interface <b>230</b> is a keyboard, touchpad, subject monitoring device, and/or other device configured to receive input. For example, a healthcare professional may use the interface <b>230</b> to start or stop the system <b>100</b> and to modify system parameters, such as the absolute duration of the procedure, pump speed, and other parameters. The interface <b>230</b> may also include a display, speaker, or other device for sending user-detectable signals. In certain implementations, the interface <b>230</b> may comprise a network interface configured to send communications to other devices. For example, the interface <b>230</b> may enable the filtration system <b>102</b> to communicate with other filtration systems, flow control devices, a server, and/or other devices.</div>
    <div id="p-0041" num="0040" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>2</b>D</figref> illustrates a segment of the filter <b>226</b> according to certain implementations, including a first section <b>256</b>, a membrane <b>258</b>, and a second section <b>260</b>, with arrows indicating flow direction. As shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>2</b>D</figref>, the filter <b>226</b> is configured as a tangential flow filter. In this configuration, the fluid <b>202</b> may enter the filter <b>206</b> and pass through the first section <b>256</b>. While the fluid <b>262</b> travels through the first section <b>256</b>, the fluid <b>262</b> may encounter the membrane <b>258</b>. A particular pressure, flow rate, or other environmental condition within the first section <b>256</b> and/or second section <b>260</b> may draw or otherwise encourage fluid to contact the membrane <b>258</b>. The environmental condition may be created by, for example, the shape, size, or configuration of the filter <b>226</b>. The environment may also be created as a result of the pump <b>222</b> or other feature of the filtration system <b>102</b> or system <b>100</b>. As a result, certain components of the fluid <b>262</b> (for example, components <b>252</b>) may pass through an aperture of the membrane <b>258</b> to the second section <b>260</b>. However, certain other components (for example, contaminants <b>254</b>) may be improperly sized (for example, the certain other components are too large) to pass through the membrane <b>258</b> and instead remain within the first section <b>256</b>. The fluid <b>262</b> that passes through the membrane <b>258</b> into the second section <b>260</b> may be described as the permeate and may pass through to the permeate outlet <b>108</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0042" num="0041" class="description-paragraph">As a specific example, the fluid <b>262</b> may be CSF having particular desirable components <b>252</b>. The CSF may also contain contaminants <b>254</b>, such as blood cells, blood cell fragments, hemolysis components, neutrophils, eosinophils, inflammatory cells, proteins, misfolded proteins, cytokines, bacteria, fungi, viruses, small and large molecules, oligomers (such as Aβ oligomers, tau oligomers, α-synuclein oligomers, and Huntingtin oligomers), antibodies (such as anti-myelin antibodies), enzymes, mutated enzymes (such as mutations to SOD1), and/or other substances. The contaminants <b>254</b> may, but need not, include materials or matter that are present in CSF normally (e.g. a cytokine that is present in CSF normally but is present in an elevated or otherwise undesirable amount). One or more of the contaminants <b>254</b> may be associated with or suspected to be associated with one or more diseases or conditions. For example, the contaminants <b>254</b> may be associated with one or more of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, Huntington's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, for instance, as described in U.S. application Ser. No. 13/801,215. The filter <b>226</b> may be used to separate the contaminants <b>254</b> from the fluid and/or desirable components <b>252</b> of the CSF. For instance, a membrane <b>258</b> may be sized or otherwise configured to allow CSF to flow through the membrane <b>258</b> while substantially preventing contaminants <b>254</b> from passing through the membrane <b>258</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0043" num="0042" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>3</b> </figref> illustrates a system <b>300</b> for the filtration of materials from biologic fluids according to certain embodiments. The system <b>300</b> may include additional components, such as but not limited to one or more flow (or pressure) regulators <b>118</b>, <b>318</b>, combiner <b>116</b>, and filtration system <b>302</b> (for example, as described in reference to filtration system <b>102</b>). Filtration system <b>302</b> may include an intake <b>304</b> (for example, as described above in reference to intake <b>104</b>), a retentate outlet <b>306</b> (for example, as described in reference to retentate outlet <b>106</b>), and a permeate outlet <b>308</b> (for example, as described above in reference to permeate outlet <b>108</b>). The arrows represent flow direction.</div>
    <div id="p-0044" num="0043" class="description-paragraph">In certain implementations, system <b>300</b> includes the filtration system <b>102</b> and, rather than having the retentate outlet <b>106</b> connected directly to the vessel <b>310</b>, the retentate outlet <b>106</b> may be connected first to a flow regulator <b>118</b> and then to the intake <b>304</b> of the second filtration system <b>302</b>. The permeate outlet <b>108</b> and permeate outlet <b>308</b> may be connected via a combiner <b>116</b> for flow to the reservoir <b>112</b>. However, the permeate outlets <b>108</b>, <b>308</b> need not necessarily be combined and may return via separate pathways to the reservoir <b>112</b>. The retentate outlet <b>306</b> may be connected to the vessel <b>310</b> via a flow regulator <b>318</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0045" num="0044" class="description-paragraph">The flow regulators <b>118</b>, <b>318</b> may be devices configured to regulate one or more fluid flow characteristics of the system <b>300</b>. These characteristics may include but are not limited to flow rate, direction, and pressure. While the flow regulators <b>118</b>, <b>318</b> are illustrated as components outside of the filtration systems <b>102</b>, <b>302</b>, they need not be or need only be located outside of the filtration systems <b>102</b>, <b>302</b> or in the exact locations illustrated. In certain embodiments, the flow regulators <b>118</b>, <b>318</b> may be located within the filtration systems <b>102</b>, <b>302</b>. In certain implementations, the filtration systems <b>102</b>, <b>302</b> or other portions of the systems <b>100</b>, <b>300</b> may include additional flow regulators. The flow regulator may include various components or subsystems for controlling flow characteristics and may include pressure regulators, backpressure regulators, sensors, and/or other devices. The flow regulators may be controllable by other components of the system (e.g., processing unit <b>228</b>).</div>
    <div id="p-0046" num="0045" class="description-paragraph">The combiner <b>116</b> may be a device in which the fluid from two or more tubes <b>112</b> is combined into a single fluid flow. For example, as illustrated in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>3</b> </figref>, the combiner <b>116</b> takes in fluid from the permeate outlet <b>108</b> and the permeate outlet <b>308</b> and combines the fluid into a single length of tubing <b>114</b> for deposit within the reservoir <b>112</b>. In some embodiments, the combiner <b>116</b> may be a simple junction that places the flow from the outlets <b>108</b>, <b>308</b> in fluid connection with the tubing <b>114</b> leading to the reservoir <b>112</b>. In some embodiments, the combiner <b>116</b> may facilitate the mixing of the fluid. In certain embodiments, the combiner <b>116</b> may also include a mechanism for flow regulation. For example, the combiner <b>116</b> may smooth turbulent flow, buffer fluid for smooth deposit within the reservoir <b>112</b>, remove air bubbles from the fluid, and perform other flow regulation or fluid treatment. The combiner <b>116</b> may also regulate the flow, direction, and pressure rate of the fluid being deposited within the reservoir <b>112</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0047" num="0046" class="description-paragraph">The filtration system <b>302</b> may be a filtration system as described above in reference to filtration system <b>102</b>. However, the filtration systems <b>102</b>, <b>302</b> may be different. For example, the filtration system <b>102</b> may be configured to filter a particular kind of contaminant <b>254</b> while the filtration system <b>302</b> may be configured to filter a different kind of contaminant <b>254</b>. In other embodiments, the filters may provide selective or progressive filtration, such as by having one set of pore sizes in filtration system <b>102</b> and then a set of smaller pore sizes in filtration system <b>302</b>, such as to provide increased filtration of the same or different contaminants <b>254</b> and/or other substance or materials. One or both filtration systems <b>102</b>, <b>302</b> may use tangential flow filtration, other filtration, or combinations thereof.</div>
    <div id="p-0048" num="0047" class="description-paragraph"> <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>4</b> </figref> illustrates a method <b>400</b> for using a filtration system for the filtration of materials from biologic fluids, including the steps of starting the process <b>402</b>, withdrawing a volume of fluid <b>404</b>, filtering and/or otherwise treating the volume of fluid <b>406</b>, measuring characteristics <b>408</b>, returning a volume of fluid <b>410</b>, determining <b>412</b>, updating parameters <b>414</b>, and ending the process <b>416</b>. The method may be utilized with certain embodiments, including system <b>100</b> and system <b>300</b>. While the method will be described with reference to system <b>300</b>, a person of skill in the art would be able to modify the steps in order to be used with other systems, including but not limited to system <b>100</b> or various combinations of systems.</div>
    <div id="p-0049" num="0048" class="description-paragraph">While the method is described as being performed on a particular volume of fluid, the system may operate on a continuous flow of fluid. That is, the system <b>300</b> need not necessarily withdraw a volume of fluid, wait for the volume to be processed and returned, and then withdraw another volume of fluid. The method may follow a continuous process. Similarly, while <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>4</b> </figref> appears to illustrate a series of consecutive steps, the steps of the described method may occur concurrently. For example, the system <b>300</b> may concurrently perform some or all of the steps illustrated in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>4</b> </figref>. For instance, the system <b>300</b> may concurrently withdraw and return fluid.</div>
    <div id="p-0050" num="0049" class="description-paragraph">The method <b>400</b> may begin at start <b>402</b>. This step <b>402</b> may include activating one or more components of the system <b>300</b>. This step <b>402</b> may also include or follow various preparation steps. Such steps may include installing filtration components, selecting and preparing the reservoir <b>112</b>, installing tubing <b>114</b>, calibrating components, priming components of the system <b>300</b>, and other steps.</div>
    <div id="p-0051" num="0050" class="description-paragraph">The installing filtration components step may include selecting particular filtration components based on desired outcomes, the particular reservoir <b>112</b>, fluid, or other considerations. For example, if the method <b>400</b> is being used on a subject suffering from a cerebral vasospasm, the goal of the procedure may be to filter blood breakdown products from the subject's CSF. This would make the reservoir <b>112</b> a lumen carrying CSF, the fluid. As such, particular filtration components would be selected to filter the blood components from the CSF. For example, a membrane <b>258</b> with apertures sized to substantially prevent the flow of blood components, while large enough to substantially allow the entry of CSF as permeate, may be used.</div>
    <div id="p-0052" num="0051" class="description-paragraph">The selecting and preparing the reservoir <b>112</b> step may include choosing a particular reservoir <b>112</b>. For example, a healthcare professional may select an individual who may benefit from having filtration performed on a bodily fluid and identify a reservoir containing the fluid. This may include, as described above, a subject suffering from a cerebral vasospasm. Preparing the reservoir <b>112</b> may include identifying an anatomical location for a procedure to access the reservoir <b>112</b> (for example, in a spinal portion <b>200</b>, as shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>2</b>A</figref>), sterilizing the location, or otherwise preparing the reservoir <b>112</b> for the procedure. Selecting and preparing the reservoir <b>112</b> may be performed according to the systems and methods described within this application or through other means. For example, selecting and preparing the reservoir <b>112</b> may be performed according to the various systems and methods described in U.S. Provisional Application No. 62/038,998.</div>
    <div id="p-0053" num="0052" class="description-paragraph">Installing tubing <b>114</b> may include connecting various components of the system <b>300</b>. For example, retentate outlet <b>106</b> may be connected to flow regulator <b>118</b>, flow regulator <b>118</b> to intake <b>304</b>, and so on. This step may also include installing tubing <b>114</b> to withdraw fluid from and return fluid to the reservoir <b>112</b>. This step may include inserting a multi-lumen catheter into an anatomical location to place the reservoir <b>112</b> in fluid connection with the system <b>300</b> to enable fluid to be drawn into the intake <b>104</b> and returned to the reservoir <b>112</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0054" num="0053" class="description-paragraph">Calibrating components may include setting initial parameters for the use of the system <b>300</b>. This step may include establishing an initial flow rate, an initial pressure, and other initial parameters or system settings. The initial parameters may be based on observed or predicted clinical measures, including but not limited to an estimated amount of fluid in the reservoir <b>112</b>, the health of the subject, the predicted ratio of retentate to permeate, and other factors.</div>
    <div id="p-0055" num="0054" class="description-paragraph">Priming the system <b>300</b> may include adding a priming solution to one or more of the components of the system <b>300</b>. Depending on the configuration of the system <b>300</b>, priming may be necessary for one or more components to function effectively. Depending on the reservoir <b>112</b>, fluid, and the subject, priming may be necessary to assure comfort or good health. In certain applications, the system <b>300</b> may be primed to enable the return of a volume of fluid while simultaneously withdrawing a volume of fluid. This may be especially useful for applications where the reservoir <b>112</b> has a relatively small volume of fluid (e.g., during filtration of CSF) or is otherwise sensitive to relative changes in volume. Depending on the type of filtration being used, the length of the procedure, and other factors, priming fluid may be added during the filtration procedure to make up for fluid lost during the procedure</div>
    <div id="p-0056" num="0055" class="description-paragraph">At step <b>404</b>, a volume of fluid is withdrawn from the reservoir <b>112</b>. In certain circumstances, the fluid may be withdrawn using a pump or device located within the system <b>100</b>. For example, the pump may be a component of one or more of the flow regulators <b>118</b>, <b>318</b>; the filtration systems <b>102</b>, <b>302</b> (such as pump <b>222</b>); and/or the combiner <b>116</b>. The pump may be used to withdraw a volume of fluid from the reservoir <b>112</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0057" num="0056" class="description-paragraph">In some embodiments, the rate at which the fluid is withdrawn from the reservoir <b>112</b> is between approximately 0.01 mL/min and approximately 100 mL/min. In preferable embodiments, the fluid rate may be 0.1 mL/min to approximately 10 mL/min. However, the amount withdrawn may be higher or lower depending on the application. The amount may vary depending on various factors including but not to the type of fluid being withdrawn, the viscosity of the fluid, the amount of fluid in the reservoir <b>112</b>, and other factors. The viscosity of the fluid may vary over time, and depending on the particular subject. For example, the viscosity of CSF may be different in a subject with meningitis than a subject with typical CSF. Once the fluid is withdrawn from the reservoir <b>112</b>, the fluid may pass through the tubing <b>114</b> and into the filtration system <b>102</b> via intake <b>104</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0058" num="0057" class="description-paragraph">At step <b>406</b>, the volume of fluid is filtered. This may include the steps of passing the fluid through a filter of the filtration system <b>102</b>. While tangential flow filters have been described in this disclosure, they need not be the filter used, or need not be the only filter used. For example, the filtration system <b>102</b> may include various filtration component configurations including but not limited to tangential flow filtration, microfiltration, ultrafiltration, nanofiltration, dead-end filters, depth filters, and other filtration devices or mechanisms.</div>
    <div id="p-0059" num="0058" class="description-paragraph">The filtration process may result in the separation of the fluid into a retentate flow and a permeate flow. The permeate flow may leave the filtration system <b>102</b> through a permeate outlet <b>108</b> and the retentate may leave the filtration system <b>102</b> through a retentate outlet <b>106</b>. Depending on the configuration of the filters and the goals of the method <b>400</b>, in some implementations, the permeate may be the fluid to be returned to the reservoir <b>112</b>. In other implementations, the retentate may be returned to the reservoir <b>112</b>. The retentate may be a fluid that contains contaminants or is otherwise in a condition undesirable for returning to the reservoir <b>112</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0060" num="0059" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, for example, as shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>3</b> </figref>, the retentate may be successively or progressively treated, such as by being filtered again through another filter process or by being filtered again through the same filter by being redirected through it. For example, in certain implementations, the retentate may be passed through a flow regulator <b>118</b> and into filtration system <b>302</b> for additional filtration. This filtration may result in the retentate being further separated into a second retentate and a second permeate. The second permeate may flow from the permeate outlet <b>308</b> to combiner <b>116</b> for return to the reservoir <b>112</b>. The second retentate may be further filtered or purified. Once the fluid is sufficiently filtered, the remaining retentate or contaminants may be passed through a flow regulator <b>318</b> and into a vessel <b>310</b> for analysis, disposal, storage, or other use, or, alternatively, or in addition, the remaining retentate may be subjected to further processing, treatment, and/or filtration (any number of times), where the further treated fluid is, for example, directed to reservoir <b>112</b>, either directly or in combination with other fluids.</div>
    <div id="p-0061" num="0060" class="description-paragraph">At step <b>408</b>, characteristics of the fluid and/or the system may be measured. Measuring characteristics may include intermittent or continuous sampling and/or monitoring of characteristics or parameters of interest. While this step <b>408</b> is shown as occurring after the filtration of the fluid <b>406</b>, the step <b>408</b> may take place at any point during the process <b>400</b> where useful data may be gathered.</div>
    <div id="p-0062" num="0061" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, measuring characteristics may include measuring the characteristics of the fluid withdrawn from the reservoir <b>112</b> before, during, or after filtration. The characteristics measured may include the presence or amount of particular contaminants, proteins, compounds, markers, and other fluid components present. As another example, the ratio of permeate volume to retentate volume, the fluid flow rate from the reservoir <b>112</b>, fluid temperature, fluid opacity or translucency or transparency, an absolute retentate flow rate, and the rate of fluid flow to the reservoir <b>112</b> also may be measured. The performance characteristics of the system <b>300</b> may also be measured. For example, the efficiency of the filter <b>226</b>, the status of the filter <b>226</b> (for example, via the interface <b>210</b>), and other markers of system <b>300</b> performance.</div>
    <div id="p-0063" num="0062" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, the characteristics measured may include information about a subject or input by a healthcare provider. For example, the system <b>300</b> may monitor the blood pressure, heart rate, stress, and other information of the subject. In addition to quantitative characteristics, qualitative measurements may be made as well. For instance, subject discomfort and other qualities may be measured. These and other data may be measured by the sensor <b>224</b> and/or be input into the system by an input device (for example, keyboard, touch screen, subject-monitoring device, and other devices for receiving input) operably coupled to the system <b>300</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0064" num="0063" class="description-paragraph">At step <b>410</b>, a volume of fluid is returned to the reservoir <b>112</b>. In certain embodiments, the fluid is returned to the reservoir <b>112</b> as soon as fluid filtration has been completed. In certain embodiments, the flow rate of the fluid may be controlled. For example, a volume of fluid may be buffered at the combiner <b>116</b> or in another area of the system <b>300</b> for a time before being returned to the reservoir <b>112</b>. Buffering may be used to smooth the return rate of the fluid, to allow time for the fluid to reach a particular temperature, to allow time for a particular additive to mix within the fluid, and for other reasons.</div>
    <div id="p-0065" num="0064" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, the rate and/or pressure at which the fluid is returned to the reservoir <b>112</b> is controlled (for example, by the combiner <b>116</b> and/or the flow regulator <b>318</b>). For example, the return of fluid is controlled so that the fluid is returned at such a rate or in such a manner as to maintain homeostasis within the reservoir <b>112</b>. In certain embodiments, this may be accomplished by returning fluid at the same rate at which fluid is currently being withdrawn from the system. In certain embodiments, the fluid may be returned at substantially the same flow rate at which it was removed. The fluid volume removed from the system and returned to the system may not be equal. This may be the case when removing a significant quantity of contaminants from a reservoir. In certain embodiments, the difference may be made up through the addition of additional fluid.</div>
    <div id="p-0066" num="0065" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, a particular volume of additional fluid may be returned to the reservoir <b>112</b>. The additional fluid may be fluid that was not withdrawn from the reservoir <b>112</b>, previously withdrawn from the reservoir <b>112</b>, withdrawn from a different reservoir, synthetically created, or is otherwise different from the volume removed from the reservoir <b>112</b> in step <b>404</b>. The return of additional fluid may be used to, for example, compensate for the volume of fluid that was filtered out, especially in circumstances where the reservoir <b>112</b> comprised only a small amount of fluid at the start <b>402</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0067" num="0066" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, one or more therapeutic agents may be added to the fluid prior to its return to the reservoir <b>112</b>. The fluid may be treated or mixed with a particular pharmacological agent. For example, when the fluid is CSF, the agent may be configured to bypass the blood-brain barrier. The agents may include, but need not be limited to, antibiotics, nerve growth factor, anti-inflammatory agents, pain-relief agents, agents designed to be delivered using intrathecal means, agents designed to affect a particular condition (e.g., meningitis, Alzheimer's disease, depression, chronic pain, and other conditions), and other agents.</div>
    <div id="p-0068" num="0067" class="description-paragraph">As a specific example, the reservoir <b>112</b> may be a C SF-containing space of a subject, such as the subarachnoid space or another space known or thought to contain CSF. The space may only have a total of approximately 125 ml of CSF, and if the level drops below a certain threshold (for example, approximately 85 ml), the subject may suffer undesirable side effects. If a particular large amount of the existing CSF comprises undesirable compounds, the volume of permeate may be small enough to cause the fluid levels in the reservoir <b>112</b> to drop below the threshold. Consequently, the system <b>300</b> may return a volume of additional fluid (for example, artificial CSF or other suitable fluid) to adjust for the difference between the amount of withdrawn CSF being returned and the amount needed to be returned in order to maintain the volume of the reservoir <b>112</b> above the threshold amount.</div>
    <div id="p-0069" num="0068" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, the withdrawal and return of the fluid may occur in a pulsed manner. For example, the system <b>300</b> may withdraw a particular volume and then cease withdrawing additional fluid. The withdrawn volume is processed by the filtration or other systems and be buffered (for example, at the combiner <b>116</b>). Filtered amount from the buffer may be returned to the reservoir <b>112</b> at about the same rate and/or for the about same total volume as a next volume is withdrawn from the reservoir <b>112</b>. This process may allow the system to maintain reservoir <b>112</b> volume levels relatively consistent and may be useful in circumstances where the processing time (for example, the time between the fluid being withdrawn from and returned to the reservoir <b>112</b>) is long.</div>
    <div id="p-0070" num="0069" class="description-paragraph">At step <b>412</b>, a determination is made. The determination may be made by, for example, a healthcare professional, a processor system, or a combination thereof. For example, the healthcare professional may analyze the measure characteristics and come to a conclusion. As another example, the processing unit <b>208</b> may analyze the measured characteristics based using an algorithm or through other mechanisms. The determination may be based on the measured parameters, a timer, a schedule, or other mechanisms. The determination may be used in order to change the parameters of the system <b>300</b> to change over time and to address particular measured characteristics.</div>
    <div id="p-0071" num="0070" class="description-paragraph">For example, a determination may be made regarding the flow rate at which the fluid is being withdrawn and/or returned to the reservoir <b>112</b>. For example, it may be desirable to maintain substantially the same withdrawal and return rate of the fluid. Specifically, if more fluid is being withdrawn from the reservoir <b>112</b> than is being returned, then the volume of fluid in the reservoir <b>112</b> may be decreasing overall. This may be undesirable because for certain fluids and certain reservoirs <b>112</b>, if the volume of the reservoir <b>112</b> passes a particular threshold, undesirable side effects may occur. For instance, where the fluid being withdrawn is CSF, the flow rate may be such that the volume of CSF removed from a human subject does not exceed about between approximately 5 mL and approximately 20 mL over the course of one hour. That is, the volume of fluid does not decrease more than approximately 5 mL to approximately 20 mL from its original starting volume in a one hour period of time. In certain embodiments, it may be desirable to maintain an absolute retentate flow rate within a certain range of acceptable retentate flow rates. In certain embodiments, the threshold may be between approximately 0.10 mL/min and approximately 0.30 mL/min. In certain embodiments, the threshold may be approximately 0.16 mL/min. In certain embodiments, the threshold may be between approximately 0.2 mL/min and approximately 0.25 mL/min; however, other values may be desirable in certain circumstances. In certain embodiments, a pump may be running at approximately 1.0 mL/min and the retentate flow rate is approximately 0.25 mL/min, the permeate flow rate is approximately 0.75 mL/min, which is about a 3:1 ratio. However, if the pump speed were increased to approximately 2.0 mL/min, the retentate flow rate may be held at approximately 0.25 mL/min, which leaves the permeate flow rate as approximately 1.75 mL/min, or about a7:1 ratio. By maintaining the retentate flow rate within the threshold, the system may be considering functioning as intended, despite the change in ratios.</div>
    <div id="p-0072" num="0071" class="description-paragraph">Based on the measured characteristics, it may be determined that the best way to address the disparity in the withdrawal and return rates may be to decrease the flow rate to reduce the overall volume of fluid lost from the system. This may mean that, although there is a net loss of fluid from the reservoir <b>112</b>, the loss is occurring at a slower rate. The rate may be sufficiently slow that, for example, that the subject's body produces sufficient fluid to make up for the loss.</div>
    <div id="p-0073" num="0072" class="description-paragraph">For example, at the beginning of the filtration process <b>400</b>, the fluid may contain large amounts of contaminants, resulting in a comparatively large amount of material being filtered out and a comparatively small amount of the fluid being returned (for example, permeate). As the filtration or treatment process continues, the amount of fluid being treated may decrease because the contaminants have already been filtered out (for example, retentate). In this scenario, a determination may be made to begin the process at a relatively low flow rate and then increase it as the volume of the fluid being filtered out decreases. In addition, the determination may include altering the flow and/or pressure within the filter <b>226</b> in order to achieve particular filtering results.</div>
    <div id="p-0074" num="0073" class="description-paragraph">As another example, the measured characteristics may be a subject's expressed discomfort. Withdrawing CSF from a CSF-containing space of a subject may cause symptoms of overdrainage, such as spinal headache. Symptoms of overdrainage may be able to be avoided or otherwise addressed by not withdrawing more than a threshold amount of CSF. However, the particular threshold may vary from subject to subject. As such, a predicted threshold may be different from an actual threshold and the subject may experience symptoms sooner than expected. In response to the subject expressing feelings of discomfort, the healthcare professional may determine that the parameters of the process may need to be changed.</div>
    <div id="p-0075" num="0074" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, at step <b>412</b>, the processing unit <b>228</b> and/or a healthcare professional may determine that the process should be completed. At this point, the flow diagram moves to end step <b>416</b>. In certain other embodiments, at step <b>412</b>, the processing unit <b>228</b> and/or a healthcare professional may determine that the process should continue substantially unchanged. Upon that determination, the flow diagram may return to step <b>404</b>. In still other embodiments, at step <b>412</b>, the processing unit <b>228</b> and/or a healthcare professional may determine that the one or more parameters of the process should be changed. Upon that determination, the flow diagram may move to step <b>414</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0076" num="0075" class="description-paragraph">At step <b>414</b>, one or more parameters of the system <b>300</b> are changed in response to a determination made in step <b>412</b>. The parameters to be changed may include inflow rate, outflow rate, buffer size, and other parameters. Such parameters may be changed via, for example, the processing unit <b>206</b> sending a signal to the pump <b>222</b> or other component of the system in order to modify the parameters. In certain embodiments, the parameters may be manually changed through input received at the input <b>208</b>. This may include parameters entered by a healthcare professional. In certain embodiments, parameters may be updated based on the difference between the withdrawal volume and the returned volume (e.g., a waste rate).</div>
    <div id="p-0077" num="0076" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, the updating parameters step <b>414</b> may include changing the flow direction of the fluid. For example, a system may include a plurality of filtration systems, which the fluid may be directed to by the manipulation of a valve or other mechanisms for changing fluid flow direction. Step <b>414</b> may include changing the fluid flow from one filtration system to a different filtration. This may be in response to determining that a second filtration system (for example, filtration system <b>302</b>) is more suited for filtering particular contaminants than a first filtration system (for example, filtration system <b>102</b>).</div>
    <div id="p-0078" num="0077" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, the updating parameters step <b>414</b> may include modifying the positioning of the tubing at the reservoir <b>112</b>. For example, one or more inflow or outflow tubes <b>114</b> may become clogged or otherwise be operating at a reduced capacity. In response, the tubing <b>114</b> may be adjusted or otherwise modified to address the reduced capacity issue. The healthcare professional may be alerted to the issue by a light, alarm or other indicia.</div>
    <div id="p-0079" num="0078" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, the updating parameters step <b>414</b> may include cleaning or otherwise modifying one or more components of the system <b>300</b>, such as the filter <b>226</b>. This may be accomplished by, for example, changing back pressure and pump speed.</div>
    <div id="p-0080" num="0079" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, the updating parameters step <b>414</b> may include sensing characteristics of the system to determine whether the filter <b>226</b> or other components of the system are experiencing clogging. The sensed characteristic may include reading an alert state of the filtration system or detecting an increase in filter pressure with no change to system flow rates or other parameters of the system. Responsive to determining that there may be a clog in the system <b>300</b>, the flow rate through the retentate port of the filters may be increased. The increased flow rate may be the result of a user or the system opening a back pressure valve (e.g., a backpressure valve of the flow regulators <b>118</b>, <b>318</b>). The opening of the valve may result in a surge of fluid through one or more retentate ports of one or more filters into a waste collection area (e.g., vessels <b>110</b>, <b>310</b>). The surge of fluid may result in the flow returning to the reservoir <b>112</b> reducing to zero or even a negative rate. Thus, the operator or system controlling the flow rate may take into account the volume of fluid lost and the possible effects on the patient as a result of this filter clearance mechanism.</div>
    <div id="p-0081" num="0080" class="description-paragraph">In certain embodiments, the updating parameters step <b>414</b> may include operating a fluid flow control method, such as a method <b>500</b> as shown in <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>5</b> </figref>. The method <b>500</b> may be used, in part, to control the flow of fluid through the system, such as the flow of retentate, permeate, waste, and/or other fluids. The fluid flow control method may include the steps of determining if the fluid flow is outside of a flow threshold <b>502</b>, determining if the flow pressure is above a pressure threshold <b>504</b>, stopping the pump <b>506</b>, tightening a backpressure valve <b>508</b>, and loosening a backpressure valve <b>510</b> (e.g., a backpressure valve of the flow regulator <b>118</b>, <b>318</b> or elsewhere within a system). While fluid is flowing through the system (e.g. system <b>100</b>, <b>300</b>), a sensor of the system may detect a fluid flow rate (e.g., the rate at which fluid is traveling to waste, such as to vessel <b>110</b>, <b>310</b>) and compare it to a threshold. If the fluid flow rate is at a threshold or within a threshold range, then no substantial changes may be needed. If the fluid flow rate is above the threshold range, then the method may proceed to step <b>504</b>. If the fluid flow is below the threshold range, then the method may proceed to step <b>510</b>. The sensing of the flow rate may be continuous or occur periodically. In certain implementations, proceeding to the step <b>504</b>, <b>510</b> need not occur immediately upon detecting a flow outside of the flow threshold; instead, the method may proceed to the step <b>504</b>, <b>510</b> after the flow is outside of the flow threshold for a particular number of checks (e.g., two or more checks of the waste flow rate). In certain embodiments, the threshold range for the fluid flow rate may be between approximately 0.2 mL/min and approximately 0.25 mL/min; however, other values may be used depending on particular implementations.</div>
    <div id="p-0082" num="0081" class="description-paragraph">Step <b>504</b> may be reached when the fluid flow is higher than the threshold flow range. At this step, it is determined whether a pressure at or of the filter is above a pressure threshold. If the pressure is above the pressure threshold, then the method moves to step <b>506</b> and the pump is stopped. If the pressure is not above the threshold, then the method moves to step <b>508</b> where a backpressure valve is tightened and the method then returns to step <b>502</b>. In certain embodiments, the threshold pressure may be 1,100 mmHg; however, other thresholds may be appropriate. Step <b>510</b> may be reached if the flow rate is lower than the flow threshold. In this step, the backflow pressure valve may be loosened and the method then returns to step <b>502</b>.</div>
    <div id="p-0083" num="0082" class="description-paragraph">Returning to <figref idrefs="DRAWINGS">FIG. <b>4</b> </figref>, at step <b>416</b>, the process comes to an end. After the process is completed, various wind-up steps may be performed, including but not limited to, applying a bandage to the subject, disassembling one or more components of the system <b>300</b>, analyzing an amount of the withdrawn fluid, analyzing the retentate, and other steps.</div>
    <div id="p-0084" num="0083" class="description-paragraph">Within this disclosure, connection references (for example, attached, coupled, connected, and joined) may include intermediate members between a collection of components and relative movement between components. Such references do not necessarily infer that two components are directly connected and in fixed relation to each other. The exemplary drawings are for purposes of illustration only and the dimensions, positions, order and relative sizes reflected in the drawings attached hereto may vary.</div>
    <div id="p-0085" num="0084" class="description-paragraph">The above specification provides a complete description of the structure and use of exemplary embodiments as claimed below. Although various embodiments of the invention as claimed have been described above with a certain degree of particularity, or with reference to one or more individual embodiments, those skilled in the art could make numerous alterations to the disclosed embodiments without departing from the spirit or scope of this disclosure. Other embodiments are therefore contemplated. It is intended that all matter contained in the above description and shown in the accompanying drawings shall be interpreted as illustrative only of particular embodiments and not limiting. Changes in detail or structure may be made without departing from the basic elements of the disclosure as defined in the following claims.</div>

  <section itemprop="claims" itemscope="">
    <h2>Claims (<span itemprop="count">10</span>)</h2>
    
    <div itemprop="content" html=""><div mxw-id="PCLM495798498" lang="EN" load-source="patent-office" class="claims">
    <claim-statement>What is claimed is:</claim-statement>
    <div class="claim"> <div id="CLM-00001" num="00001" class="claim">
      <div class="claim-text">1. A system for filtering materials from cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of a human or animal subject, the system comprising:
<div class="claim-text">a filtration system, the filtration system including a multi-lumen catheter, a pump, a first filter, a second filter, and a combiner;</div>
<div class="claim-text">a processor coupled to the filtration system;</div>
<div class="claim-text">wherein the multi-lumen catheter is configured to be inserted at least partially into a CSF-containing space of a subject for withdrawing a first volume of a fluid comprising CSF from the CSF-containing space of the subject at a first flow rate through a first lumen formed in the multi-lumen catheter;</div>
<div class="claim-text">wherein the filtration system is configured to operate according to a set of operation parameters;</div>
<div class="claim-text">wherein the first filter includes a tangential flow filter for filtering the first volume of the fluid into a first permeate and a first retentate;</div>
<div class="claim-text">wherein the second filter is configured to filter the first retentate into a second permeate and a second retentate;</div>
<div class="claim-text">wherein the combiner is configured to combine the first permeate with the second permeate to form a combined permeate;</div>
<div class="claim-text">wherein the filtration system includes one or more sensors for measuring the first volume, a volume of the combined permeate, and a difference between the first volume and a volume of the combined permeate;</div>
<div class="claim-text">wherein the multi-lumen catheter is designed to return the combined permeate through a second lumen formed in the multi-lumen catheter to the CSF-containing space of the subject at a second flow rate;</div>
<div class="claim-text">and</div>
<div class="claim-text">wherein the processor is configured to update a parameter of the set of operation parameters when the difference between the first volume and the volume of the combined permeate exceeds a predetermined threshold.</div>
</div>
    </div>
    </div> <div class="claim-dependent"> <div id="CLM-00002" num="00002" class="claim">
      <div class="claim-text">2. The system of <claim-ref idref="CLM-00001">claim 1</claim-ref>, wherein the parameter comprises the first flow rate and the second flow rate.</div>
    </div>
    </div> <div class="claim-dependent"> <div id="CLM-00003" num="00003" class="claim">
      <div class="claim-text">3. The system of <claim-ref idref="CLM-00002">claim 2</claim-ref>, wherein updating the parameter of the set of operation parameters comprises equalizing the first flow rate and the second flow rate.</div>
    </div>
    </div> <div class="claim-dependent"> <div id="CLM-00004" num="00004" class="claim">
      <div class="claim-text">4. The system of <claim-ref idref="CLM-00001">claim 1</claim-ref>, wherein the predetermined threshold is a difference between the first volume and the volume of the combined permeate that is predicted to induce a spinal headache.</div>
    </div>
    </div> <div class="claim-dependent"> <div id="CLM-00005" num="00005" class="claim">
      <div class="claim-text">5. The system of <claim-ref idref="CLM-00004">claim 4</claim-ref>, wherein the subject is a human subject and the difference between the first volume and the volume of the combined permeate that is predicted to induce a spinal headache is between about 35 milliliters per hour and 45 milliliters per hour.</div>
    </div>
    </div> <div class="claim-dependent"> <div id="CLM-00006" num="00006" class="claim">
      <div class="claim-text">6. The system of <claim-ref idref="CLM-00001">claim 1</claim-ref>, wherein the parameter of the set of operation parameters comprises a flow rate parameter and updating the parameter of the set of operation parameters causes the first and second flow rate to decrease.</div>
    </div>
    </div> <div class="claim-dependent"> <div id="CLM-00007" num="00007" class="claim">
      <div class="claim-text">7. The system of <claim-ref idref="CLM-00001">claim 1</claim-ref>, wherein the first flow rate is between approximately 0.04 milliliters per minute and approximately 30 milliliters per minute.</div>
    </div>
    </div> <div class="claim-dependent"> <div id="CLM-00008" num="00008" class="claim">
      <div class="claim-text">8. The system of <claim-ref idref="CLM-00001">claim 1</claim-ref>, wherein the filtration system includes a port for adding a therapeutic agent to the combined permeate prior to returning the combined permeate to the CSF-containing space.</div>
    </div>
    </div> <div class="claim-dependent"> <div id="CLM-00009" num="00009" class="claim">
      <div class="claim-text">9. The system of <claim-ref idref="CLM-00001">claim 1</claim-ref>, wherein the filtration system includes a port for adding artificial CSF to the combined permeate prior to returning the combined permeate to the CSF-containing space.</div>
    </div>
    </div> <div class="claim-dependent"> <div id="CLM-00010" num="00010" class="claim">
      <div class="claim-text">10. The system of <claim-ref idref="CLM-00001">claim 1</claim-ref>, further comprising:
<div class="claim-text">a second sensor for measuring is an absolute retentate flow rate;</div>
<div class="claim-text">wherein the filtration system is designed to determine whether passes a second threshold, where the second threshold is a range of acceptable retentate flow rates; and</div>
<div class="claim-text">wherein the filtration system is designed to update a second parameter of the set of operation parameters to cause the absolute retentate flow rate to return to within the range of acceptable retentate flow rates.</div>
</div>

metadata.DC.description: Systems and methods for filtering materials from biologic fluids are discussed. Embodiments may be used to filter cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from a human or animal subject. The method may include the steps of withdrawing fluid comprising CSF, filtering the volume into permeate and retentate by passing the fluid through a tangential flow filter, and returning the permeate to the subject. During operation of the system, various parameters may be modified, such as flow rate.
metadata.DC.title: Tangential flow filter system for the filtration of materials from biologic fluids

metadata.description: Systems and methods for filtering materials from biologic fluids are discussed. Embodiments may be used to filter cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from a human or animal subject. The method may include the steps of withdrawing fluid comprising CSF, filtering the volume into permeate and retentate by passing the fluid through a tangential flow filter, and returning the permeate to the subject. During operation of the system, various parameters may be modified, such as flow rate.

data.title: Tangential flow filter system for the filtration of materials from biologic fluids
